items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: I started writing music when I started with Duke Ellington.

ctx.x: Never did, huh? When did you start writing music?
Oh, I started writing music when I started with Duke Ellington.
That was the very first time you wrote?
Barry Ulanov in his book mentions that you were playing maracas as well as, clavés trombone.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...played with Duke you a couple of weeks... INTERVIEWEE: No, I don't think so.

ctx.x: I think so; I think so.

I see. Okay. I wanted to get that straight. Were you in the band at the time that Sidney Bâchet came briefly in to the band in New York? I think he only played with Duke you a couple of weeks or something.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: I know he was working for Duke and Irving Mills in the publishing company.

ctx.x: The lyric writer, perhaps, of Lost in Meditation, was Singer. There are four names; Tizol, Ellington, Singer and Mills. In Lost in Meditation. Singer? S-i-n-g-e-r.
I know he was working for Duke and Irving Mills in the publishing company.
